description: Agent Customs Records: submit tariff classification records with the invoice lines and rulings they answer to: each classification record with its id, the entry, the product or part reference, the goods as classified, the tariff line, the ruling or basis it cites and any note on the line chosen; each commercial invoice line with its id, the entry, the product reference and the goods as invoiced; each ruling or basis on file with its id, reference, the product and the tariff line it gives. The signed report gives the classifications and the goods, each item of goods across the entries it is classified on, each cited ruling or basis against the rulings on file, and each classified description against the invoice line for the same entry and goods, and counts them, and names divergent tariff classification records: the same goods classified under different tariff lines on different entries with no note, a classification record citing a ruling or basis the file does not hold, and goods described one way on the invoice and another way in the classification record; then an invoice line naming an entry no classification record holds and a classification using another tariff line than the ruling it cites gives, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No classifications, a record with no tariff line in digits, or no invoice lines leaves those points unverified. Entries, products and rulings match by letters and digits, tariff lines compare by their digits so 6109.10.0012 and 6109100012 are one line and a line read to fewer digits is another, goods with no product reference group by their words, and two descriptions agree when every word of one appears in the other with plurals folded. This reads whether each item of goods is classified one way across the importer’s entries, on a basis the file holds. Verdict customs_classification_divergent, customs_classification_partial, customs_classification_unverified or customs_classification_consistent. POST /api/customs-classification-check. Reads the customs and trade records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it files no entry, pays no duty, contacts no customs authority or broker and gives no customs or legal advice, which stay with the importer, its licensed customs broker and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Customs Records reads an importer’s or exporter’s own customs and trade records: entry summaries, tariff classification records, duty and fee payment records, broker filing records, country-of-origin and marking records, declared-value records, customs bond records and drawback claim records, each against the commercial invoices and duty payment records, the rulings on file, the entries, the importer’s own copies, the origin support on file, the invoices and payments, the entry activity or the duty recorded as paid and the proof on file. The family’s ground is the paper behind the border crossing: what was declared, how it was classified, what duty was paid, and whether the bond and the drawback claims line up; the Agent Tax Records family reads filings made to the tax authority, and the Agent Logistics family reads where a shipment is and when it moves, while this family reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-customs-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-customs-records/.
